source_row.extraction_instructions: WordPress Tribe Events site; the listing is read from /wp-json/tribe/events/v1/events (per_page=50, walks total_pages). The API record holds every field, so extract_detail works from the shell. Curated aggregator of third-party ORL congresses: booking_url is the organiser website. Same meeting is often posted twice (deduped on start_date + venue string). Fees only when Tribe cost is set, currency from cost_details.

concerns: Recon volume estimate (~160) was wrong: the API total is 16 upcoming (2 dupes removed = 14 shells). Real count proven against the API's own 'total' field.

Duplicates (Rome 6th World Congress, London World Tinnitus Congress) are deduped on start_date + venue string, keeping the record with an organiser website/cost/longest text; a legit second event on the same day at an identical venue string would be collapsed.
API is slow (~18 s per call); fetch timeout set to 90 s with 3 tries. Only 1 page is needed at per_page=50.
Only 2 of 14 events state a fee in Tribe (USD); others get no tiers. Organiser sites are third-party and not scraped.
booking_url is the organiser's own site (listing 'website'); source_url stays the ifosworld.org event URL. Tinnitus 4797 has no website so falls back to the ifosworld URL.
Specialty is hard-set to 'ENT' (federation scope) because the keyword classifier tags thyroidology as Endocrinology.
Meniere's symposium city is 'Chiyoda-ku' (Tribe's value; a Tokyo ward). Event 'ESSA' description is the site's own terse text ('4ESSA INVIT FLY ...').
Navigation of the thin /event/ wrapper page is slow and can hit the 10 s domcontentloaded timeout; extract_detail does not depend on the page.
No shared-file changes needed. tribe_events.py did not exist when built, so this builds on the API directly (not subclassed).
